_about: Budgets are ratios against a yardstick measured in the same run -- dictionary, integer and string work in a loop, never this project's code -- because seconds recorded on one machine cannot gate another, and a yardstick written in C would measure CPython releases rather than this code. One entry per operating system: the ratio does not travel between platforms either, so each carries what was measured on it, and a platform with no entry passes quietly because there is no way to write a budget for a machine before a run on it. The seconds below are for a reader; what is compared is the ratio.

Darwin._from: the mean of three consecutive runs on an idle machine, which read 126/110/115 on the corpus and 0.472/0.409/0.426 on the rules layer -- a spread of about 7%, so an ordinary run sits near 1.0x and nowhere near the warning line. Recording the lowest of the three would have put an ordinary run at 1.15x for no reason.
